c.tagline: A lagoon town on the Garden Route framed by dramatic sandstone Heads and ancient indigenous forest

card: Widely accepted in town; cash useful for markets and smaller township eateries

taxi.fare: Negotiated or metered depending on operator
taxi.fareNote: Confirm the fare or use a ride-hailing app rather than hailing an unmarked taxi

emergency.note: 112 from any mobile phone reaches all emergency services

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: The waterfront and central Knysna are walkable; the Heads, forests, and outlying beaches require a car or organized tour

safety.safety: Generally safe for tourists in the central and waterfront areas, though petty crime occurs as in most South African towns
safety.crime: Avoid isolated areas after dark and secure valuables; township areas require a local guide

hood_landmark.Knysna Central / Waterfront: The Knysna Quays waterfront shopping and dining complex
hood_landmark.Leisure Isle: Leisure Isle's lagoon-front beaches and sailing club
hood_landmark.The Heads: The Western and Eastern Heads lookout points over the lagoon mouth
hood_landmark.Brenton-on-Sea: Brenton-on-Sea's beach and Featherbed Nature Reserve views

avoid.reason: Avoid walking in the townships north of the N2 without a local guide.
Lock cars and hide valuables at trailheads and viewpoints, and avoid walking after dark away from the waterfront.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of town along the lagoon, with the Knysna Quays complex, restaurants, and oyster bars; the natural base for most visitors.
A upscale canal-front marina development a short drive from downtown, popular for its restaurants and waterfront apartments.
A residential peninsula jutting into the lagoon with quiet beaches and lawn-fringed streets, good for a calmer stay.
The dramatic sandstone cliffs flanking the lagoon's narrow entrance to the sea, essential for photos and sunset views.
A small beach village west of Knysna with dramatic coastal views over the Featherbed Nature Reserve, better for a peaceful coastal stay than nightlife.
lodging: Protea Hotel by Marriott Knysna Quays

water.note: Municipal tap water is safe; occasional drought restrictions apply.

transit.sys: No formal municipal bus network; minibus taxis serve local routes
transit.hours: Minibus taxis run roughly daylight hours
transit.map: Not centrally published; ask locally for minibus taxi routes
transit.note: Most visitors rent a car, since Garden Route sights are spread out along the N2

transport.air: George Airport (GRJ), about 1 hr drive; Cape Town International (CPT) is roughly 5 hr away by car
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Knysna
transport.bus: Greyhound, Intercape, and Baz Bus (backpacker hop-on-hop-off) connect along the Garden Route
transport.car: A rental car is strongly recommended for exploring the Garden Route; driving is on the left

airport.name: George Airport
airport.transport: Rental car, pre-booked transfer, or shuttle

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier in forest areas
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Vodacom or MTN tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is customary for tour guides and drivers

food.name: Knysna oysters
food.desc: Lagoon-grown and wild Knysna oysters served on ice with lemon, Tabasco and a dash of pepper; the town's defining food and its July festival.

places.name: The Oyster Shed
places.note: Serving oysters on the water's edge since 1979; no reservations, wooden tables, unbeatable freshness.

places.name: 34 Degrees South
places.note: Part fish market, part restaurant; shuck-to-order oysters eaten looking over the marina.

places.name: Freshline Fisheries
places.note: Sand-floored, bring-your-own-wine seafood shed locals rate for the cheapest fresh oysters in town.

food.name: Grilled line fish
food.desc: Whatever came off the boats that morning, kingklip, yellowtail, kabeljou or red roman, grilled simply with lemon butter.

places.name: Freshline Fisheries
places.note: Pick your fish from the counter and they cook it; the most honest line-fish meal on the Garden Route.

places.name: East Head Cafe
places.note: Perched above the lagoon mouth with the best view in Knysna and a long-standing seafood menu.

places.name: 34 Degrees South
places.note: Fish market attached to the restaurant means the day's catch goes straight to the grill.

food.name: Seafood platter
food.desc: A loaded board of prawns, calamari, mussels, line fish and oysters, the classic Garden Route splurge shared between two.

places.name: The Oyster Shed
places.note: Platters built around lagoon oysters and the day's catch, eaten casually beside the water.

places.name: Freshline Fisheries
places.note: Generous platters at market prices, and no corkage if you carry in your own wine.

places.name: Sirocco
places.note: Waterside deck restaurant popular for long seafood lunches and sundowners over the lagoon.

food.name: Smoked snoek
food.desc: Cape snoek hot-smoked over wood, flaked into pate or served whole with apricot jam; a South African coastal tradition.

places.name: 34 Degrees South
places.note: Deli counter stocks smoked snoek and pate alongside the fish market.

places.name: Freshline Fisheries
places.note: Sells smoked and fresh snoek over the counter as well as cooking it in the restaurant.

places.name: Wild Oats Community Farmers Market
places.note: Saturday-morning market where smokers and small producers sell snoek pate and local preserves.

food.name: Biltong and droewors
food.desc: Air-dried, coriander-spiced beef, kudu or ostrich, sliced as biltong or coiled as droewors sausage; South Africa's road-trip snack.

places.name: Wild Oats Community Farmers Market
places.note: Long-running Saturday market with several biltong and game-meat producers from the Garden Route.

places.name: 34 Degrees South
places.note: Deli section stocks biltong and droewors to nibble with a glass of Cape wine.

places.name: Main Street butcheries
places.note: Town-centre butchers slice biltong to order by weight, far cheaper than tourist-shop packets.

food.name: Melktert
food.desc: Milk tart: a pale, wobbly baked custard in a thin pastry shell, dusted with cinnamon; the Afrikaans teatime classic.

places.name: Ile de Pain
places.note: Celebrated wood-fired bakery and cafe, the best baking in Knysna and always busy at breakfast.

places.name: Wild Oats Community Farmers Market
places.note: Home bakers sell melktert, koeksisters and pancakes from early Saturday morning.

places.name: East Head Cafe
places.note: Good spot for cake and coffee with the lagoon mouth in front of you.

food.name: Mitchell's craft beer
food.desc: Beer from Knysna's own Mitchell's Brewery, one of South Africa's first craft breweries; Forester's Draught and Bosun's Bitter are the staples.

places.name: Mitchell's Brewery
places.note: The brewery taproom itself, pouring the beers it has made in Knysna since 1983.

places.name: The Oyster Shed
places.note: Cold local beer alongside the oysters, which is exactly the pairing the town is built on.

places.name: Sirocco
places.note: Waterside deck that draws a big sundowner crowd; local draught on tap.

food.name: Rooibos tea
food.desc: Naturally caffeine-free red bush tea grown only in the Western Cape, drunk plain, with milk, or iced with lemon.

places.name: Ile de Pain
places.note: Serves rooibos and good coffee with its bread and pastries in a converted boatyard building.

places.name: East Head Cafe
places.note: Rooibos with a clifftop view of the lagoon mouth; a fine mid-morning stop.

places.name: Wild Oats Community Farmers Market
places.note: Stalls sell loose rooibos and honeybush blends from Cape growers.

landmarks: Knysna Heads
Two towering sandstone cliffs guard the dramatic channel where lagoon meets ocean, delivering the Garden Route's single most spectacular viewpoint.
Featherbed Nature Reserve
A ferry-and-trailer excursion explores this private reserve on the western Head, combining coastal forest trails, sea caves and lagoon panoramas.
Knysna Waterfront (Knysna Quays)
Yachts bob beside restaurants and craft shops at this lively harbour development, the departure point for lagoon cruises and famous local oysters.
Thesen Islands
A former timber-mill island reborn as a canal-laced marina village, ideal for waterside dining, gallery browsing and stand-up paddleboarding.
Knysna Lagoon
This vast protected estuary, home to the endangered Knysna seahorse, shimmers with sailboats and sunset cruises at the town's heart.
Diepwalle Forest and Big Tree
Ancient Outeniqua yellowwoods, including an 880-year-old giant, tower over fern-filled trails in the indigenous forest that once hid Knysna's elusive elephants.
Noetzie Beach
A steep path descends to this wild, castle-studded beach where whimsical stone holiday homes overlook rolling Indian Ocean surf.
Brenton-on-Sea
A long crescent of golden sand on the lagoon's western shore, prized for whale watching, beach walks and blazing sunsets.
Knysna Elephant Park
This pioneering sanctuary for orphaned African elephants offers close encounters and feeding experiences a short drive east of town.
Jubilee Creek and the Goldfields
A gold-rush-era picnic glade in the Knysna forests, where a waterfall trail follows diggings left by 1880s prospectors.

train.note: Knysna has no working passenger railway - the much-loved Outeniqua Choo-Tjoe steam service along the coast to George was destroyed by floods in 2006 and has never been restored, though restoration is periodically discussed. The nearest Shosholoza Meyl (https://shosholozameyl.co.za/) services are far inland. Arrive by coach on the N2 or fly into George, about an hour west.

bus.note: No international coaches - Knysna is deep inside South Africa on the Garden Route. Intercape (https://www.intercape.co.za/) and the Baz Bus hop-on hop-off backpacker service (https://www.bazbus.com/) both call here, with Cape Town about 7 hours west and Port Elizabeth 3 hours east. The Baz Bus is popular because it drops at hostel doors rather than a terminal.

intl.to: Featherbed Nature Reserve & the Knysna Heads (South Africa) - across the lagoon

ferry.note: There is no scheduled international or coastal ferry - the Knysna Heads are notoriously dangerous to navigate and the lagoon is not a through route. The ferries here cross to the Featherbed reserve on the western head, which has no public road access, so the boat is the only way in; they run as timed departures with a guided tour attached.

half.name: Wilderness
half.blurb: A string of lakes, lagoons, and beach separated by forested dunes make up this national park along the Garden Route.

half.name: Plettenberg Bay
half.blurb: A beach town with dramatic sandstone cliffs and a lagoon sits along the coast east of Knysna.

half.name: Tsitsikamma National Park
half.blurb: A suspension bridge crosses the Storms River mouth where it meets the sea, framed by cliffs and indigenous forest.

full.name: Oudtshoorn
full.blurb: Ostrich farms and the Cango Caves, a limestone cave system with large calcite chambers, lie over the Outeniqua mountains from Knysna.
